column2: How do I place one of my charts everywhere (record, investigation, page layout…) and keep it up to date?
column3: A chart saved in the Chart editor has a name and can be placed everywhere: as a widget on its own or with other parts on the dashboard, and wherever there is “＋ Diagram” (block of a Note, investigation, Workshop project, page layout, table) → “📈 One of my charts” (the usual search menu: type a few letters of the name). For a person’s page or an investigation, you can also do it from the chart editor: “📌 Also place it on…”. When you change the chart (figures, drawing, colours, name), it changes everywhere it is placed; “✎ Edit” on the placed chart reopens the Chart editor.

column2: Can my charts use the timelines, slices and links of the diagrams?
column3: Yes. In the Chart editor, “Drawing” offers the simple drawings, then all the types of My diagrams: slices (pie, ring, mosaic, gauges, pictograms…), figures (columns, line, radar, pyramid, heat map…), assemblies (hemicycle…), links (word cloud) and, with a list of people, the lives timeline, the chronological timeline and the migration flow (place of birth → place of death). The types are the same on both sides: ⚙️ in the diagram gallery (Charts → My diagrams → ＋ New) (or ⚙️ Arrange the types in the gallery) for their order, to hide those you do not use and to make your own groups.

column2: Which diagrams for my genealogy (fan, sunburst, network, arcs, Venn)?
column3: In “＋ New diagram”, the “Genealogy” group offers: 🪭 the ancestry fan (half circle, three quarters or full circle, from 3 to 10 generations) where each box is coloured according to a figure or a category — research rate, region, department, occupation, century, name…; 🌞 the lineage sunburst (rings from the centre outwards, each slice sized by its figure, for example the number of descendants); 🕸 the network of relationships (witnesses, godfathers, godmothers, neighbours…: the points spread out by themselves, you can drag them, zoom with ＋ − or Ctrl + wheel, ↺ to reset to default, double-click to free a point); 🌈 the link arcs (people on a line, joined by arcs: pedigree collapse, marriages between families); ⭕ the Venn diagram of 2 to 4 sets. Each one is filled in by hand, by pasting a table, with a CSV, or through the “From the app” tab (your Sosa ancestors, a line of descendants, the witnesses of records, your labels, profiles and name groups), then adjusted, exported and placed everywhere like the others.

column2: How do I see the seasons and the long timespan of my family (calendar, month rose, spiral)?
column3: In “＋ New diagram”, “Timelines” group: 🗓 the coloured calendar (each day is a box that is darker or lighter depending on the number of events; all years together to see the season, or one row per year), 🌸 the month rose (12 slices, one per month, with several series: births, marriages, deaths…) and 🌀 the time spiral (one turn per century or per decade; a date = a point, a start and an end = a line, like a life). Dates are written as in a record: “7 May 1925”, “08/12/1960”, “12 Thermidor Year II”. The “From the app” tab takes the births, baptisms, marriages, deaths and burials of your whole database or of a person’s ancestors.

column2: Which diagrams can tell my family’s story (who knew whom, survival, occupations, marriages, pedigree collapse, births, places lived)?
column3: In “＋ New diagram”: 🤝 Who knew whom (Timelines) — the lives of several generations one under another; the app tells who knew whom, for example “your great-grandmother knew her great-grandson for 6 years”, and colours in yellow the years when the most generations were alive together; 📉 Survival curve (Figures) — the share still alive at each age, one curve per century, per sex or per branch, with the age at which half are still alive (living people count up to their age today); 🔀 Occupations from father to son (Genealogy) — bands that follow occupations over 3 to 5 generations, in green if the occupation is kept; 💍 Marriage radius (Genealogy) — one point per couple, at the distance between the two spouses’ places of birth, with one circle per century and a small table; 🧮 Pedigree collapse (Genealogy) — per generation, the possible ancestors (2, 4, 8…), the places found and the different people; 📅 Months of marriages and conceptions (Timelines) — Lent and Advent marked, conceptions = birth minus 9 months; 👶 Birth spacing (Timelines) — one row per mother, her children at the age she was, the gap in months and the children who died young; 🏘️ Timeline of places lived (Timelines) — one band per person, coloured by commune, department or country. The “From the app” tab fills them with your database (the starting person is chosen in the usual search menu); a click on a bar, a point or a month opens the record or the list of the people concerned. The occupation comes from the record or the first “Occupation” event; the marriage radius needs the coordinates of the places.

column2: How do I colour a map according to my figures (departments, regions, countries)?
column3: In “＋ New diagram”, “Maps” group: 🗺️ the map coloured by area. In Settings, choose the map (France, Belgium, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Europe, World) and its level of detail (departments, regions or communes; provinces; cantons; countries or NUTS 1 and 2 regions; countries or continents). In Data, one row per area: its name or its code (35, 2A, FRH03, VD, BE…) and its figure; you can paste a table or import a CSV, and rows that are not found are flagged under the map. “From the app” counts your births, marriages or deaths (or only those of your ancestors, over a period): each place in your database is attached to its area according to its coordinates. Gradient or class colours, labels, legend; the value shows on hover. The overseas territories are in insets.

column2: How do I choose the part of the world a map shows?
column3: In the preview of a map: the wheel zooms, dragging moves, Shift + drag (or “▭ Draw a frame”) frames an area, “↺ Reset to default” goes back to the starting frame. This framing is saved with the diagram. In Settings, “Part of the map” also offers ready-made frames (Western Europe, Mediterranean, North America, North Africa, Indian Ocean, Caribbean, Quebec and Acadia… or, for France, Brittany-Normandy, South-West, Corsica…) and “Projection” the drawing of the globe (Equal Earth or Robinson for the world, Lambert for Europe).

column2: How do I draw my family’s migrations on a map?
column3: In “＋ New diagram”, “Maps” group: 🧭 the migration map. Each row is a flow “departure → arrival → how many”; the arrow is thicker when there are more people. “From the app” takes from your database the place of birth → place of death, birth → marriage, or from one generation to the next (parent’s birth → child’s birth), possibly for your ancestors only. “Add a flow” lets you choose the two places with the place search menu; a place without a position is chosen in “The places in the table”, found automatically (🔎) or typed with its coordinates (“Brest 48.39, -4.49”). Same backgrounds and same framing as the coloured map.

column2: How do I colour the communes (towns) on a map, or see Paris in large?
column3: In the map coloured by area, Settings → “Level of detail” → “Communes (towns)”, for France (overseas included), Belgium, Switzerland and Luxembourg. One row per commune: its INSEE (35238) or official code, or its name; if there are several communes with the same name (Saint-Martin…), add the department: “Saint-Martin (Gers)”, “Saint-Martin 32”; otherwise the row is flagged “namesakes” under the map. The arrondissements of Paris, Lyon and Marseille and the former merged communes are recognised. “From the app” attaches each place by its INSEE code, then its name and department. To see the communes of a single department, choose “Part of the map” → “Zoom on a department…” and type its name or number. On maps of France, “Zoomed inset on Île-de-France” shows Paris and the inner suburbs (or the whole region) in large in a free corner (under the map on a phone), with the same colours, labels and tooltips.

column2: How do I see on a map where my ancestors were born (or married, died), one point per event?
column3: In “＋ New diagram”, “Maps” group: 📍 the point map (one point per event, coloured by kind or by century; the points of the same place spread out in a spiral) or ⬢ the hexagon map (the map cut into equal cells, darker where there are more events; cell size in Settings). “From the app” tab: births, deaths, marriages, residences or one kind of event, only your ancestors, between two years; places without coordinates are found among the communes of France, and “🔎 Find places without a position” looks for the others. A click on a point or a cell opens the record, or the list of people.

column2: How do I make a distorted map, where departments grow according to the number of ancestors?
column3: In “＋ New diagram”, “Maps” group: 🫧 the distorted map (cartogram). Each department, region or country becomes a circle (or a square) whose size follows its figure, placed near its real position, with the real map faintly underneath. “From the app” → “Different people” + “Only my ancestors” gives the number of ancestors per area. Settings: shape, size, colours, labels.

column2: How do I tell an ancestor’s life on a map, step by step?
column3: In “＋ New diagram”, “Maps” group: 📖 the storytelling map. “From the app”: choose the person, their events become the steps. Under the drawing: ◀ ▶, ▶︎ play and the slider move the life forward; the map follows the step (or shows the whole life, Settings → “The map”), the path already travelled is in red, the timeline at the bottom shows the years; a click on a step of the timeline goes there.

column2: What other drawings are there for descendants, godparents and causes of death?
column3: In “＋ New diagram”, “Genealogy” group: 🧱 descendants as rectangles (each child under their parent, width = number of descendants; click = the record); 🎀 names passed on (godfather or godmother → godchild who bears their first name, one row per name, colour according to the relationship: grandfather, uncle, sister…; “From the app” reads the “godfather” and “godmother” witnesses of births and baptisms); 🎗 causes of death as rings (the large groups in the centre, guessed from the words of the record, the details around; click = the list of people). The cause is noted in the “Cause” field of a death.
